scr_budgeting_departments.purpose: Explains departments — an optional dimension (e.g., Leasing, Maintenance, Administration, Amenities) used to filter and categorize transactions and budgets within a property.
scr_budgeting_departments.outcome: Budgets and actuals can be analyzed by department, showing which team drives cost.
scr_budgeting_departments.rootCause: Large or mixed-use properties want to know whether a cost overrun came from maintenance or leasing. Department tagging answers that without splitting the chart of accounts into dozens of department-specific accounts.
scr_budgeting_departments.ifSkipped: Cost overruns cannot be attributed to a team and the chart of accounts is bloated with department variants.
redFlags: Transactions posted without departments at properties that budget by department

scr_budgeting_importing_departments.purpose: Imports department records from a template, used when rolling out departmental reporting across a portfolio.
scr_budgeting_importing_departments.outcome: Consistent department codes loaded across all properties in one step.
scr_budgeting_importing_departments.rootCause: Departmental reporting only works if every property uses the same codes. Importing a standard list avoids each property creating its own variations.
scr_budgeting_importing_departments.ifSkipped: Department codes differ between properties and portfolio-level department reports cannot be produced.

scr_budgeting_departments_list.purpose: Lists department records available for budgeting and posting, with actions to add, edit and delete.
scr_budgeting_departments_list.outcome: A maintained set of departments for tagging budgets and transactions.
scr_budgeting_departments_list.rootCause: Department lists drift as staff create ad hoc departments; reviewing the list keeps departmental reports clean and comparable.
scr_budgeting_departments_list.ifSkipped: Ad hoc departments fragment reporting and make departmental BVA unreliable.

scr_budgeting_adding_and_editing_departm.purpose: Adds or edits a department record — code, name, parent — for use in budgets and transaction coding.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_editing_departm.outcome: New organizational units can be budgeted and tracked.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_editing_departm.rootCause: Operating model changes (a new amenities team, centralized leasing) need new departments so their costs are visible separately from existing teams.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_editing_departm.ifSkipped: New teams' costs are mixed into existing departments and cannot be evaluated.
redFlags: Department renames that change historical reports

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_department.purpose: Deletes a department that has no transactions or budgets, such as one created in error.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_department.outcome: Unused departments removed without affecting history.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_department.rootCause: Unused departments are selected by mistake and scatter costs into codes nobody reports on; departments with history must be kept or inactivated instead.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_department.ifSkipped: Costs are coded to meaningless departments and drop out of departmental reports.

scr_budgeting_department_information_pag.purpose: The department record page with code, name, parent department and status, defining how a department such as Maintenance rolls up under Operations in departmental budget and BVA reports.
scr_budgeting_department_information_pag.outcome: Complete department definitions that roll up correctly in reports.
scr_budgeting_department_information_pag.rootCause: Parent relationships determine how departments roll up (e.g., Maintenance under Operations); wrong parents put costs in the wrong subtotal.
scr_budgeting_department_information_pag.ifSkipped: Departmental subtotals are wrong because departments roll into the wrong parent.
redFlags: Departments without parent assignment in a hierarchy

scr_budgeting_locations.purpose: Explains locations — the dimension representing properties (and often buildings or phases) organized in a hierarchy of regions, portfolios and owners.
scr_budgeting_locations.outcome: Budgets and actuals roll up from property to region, owner and fund.
scr_budgeting_locations.rootCause: Institutional reporting is hierarchical: asset managers review by fund, regional managers by region, site teams by property. The location hierarchy makes those roll-ups automatic.
scr_budgeting_locations.ifSkipped: Regional and fund-level budget reports must be assembled by hand.
redFlags: Properties not placed in the hierarchy

scr_budgeting_importing_locations.purpose: Imports location records from a CSV file, used when onboarding a portfolio of properties.
scr_budgeting_importing_locations.outcome: Many properties created consistently with their hierarchy.
scr_budgeting_importing_locations.rootCause: Portfolio take-overs bring dozens of properties at once; importing them with parents avoids manual setup errors.
scr_budgeting_importing_locations.ifSkipped: Properties are created manually with inconsistent codes and parents.

scr_budgeting_locations_list.purpose: Lists the locations (properties, buildings, phases) available to Forecasting & Planning with their parent in the hierarchy and active status, used to confirm every property can be budgeted.
scr_budgeting_locations_list.outcome: A view of all properties that budgets can be built for.
scr_budgeting_locations_list.rootCause: Before budget season, confirming every active property exists as a location avoids missing budgets for newly acquired properties.
scr_budgeting_locations_list.ifSkipped: New properties have no budget because they were never set up as locations.

scr_budgeting_adding_and_editing_locatio.purpose: Adds or edits a location — code, name, parent, entity and status — for use in budgets and transactions.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_editing_locatio.outcome: Properties set up correctly in the reporting hierarchy.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_editing_locatio.rootCause: A location placed under the wrong parent or entity rolls its budget and actuals into the wrong owner's reports.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_editing_locatio.ifSkipped: Budgets and actuals roll into the wrong owner or region.
redFlags: Locations mapped to the wrong entity

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_location.purpose: Deletes a location record that never received transactions or budgets — for example a property code created twice during onboarding — while locations with history are inactivated instead.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_location.outcome: Unused locations removed without affecting reporting history.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_location.rootCause: Locations with history must be inactivated rather than deleted; deleting is only safe for records that never received transactions or budgets.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_location.ifSkipped: Erroneous locations remain selectable and receive postings by mistake.

scr_budgeting_location_information_page.purpose: The location record page holding the property's code, name, parent in the hierarchy, legal entity, address and status, which together determine how its budget and actuals roll up.
scr_budgeting_location_information_page.rootCause: Entity and parent on this page drive how each property's budget and actuals roll up into owner and fund reports.
scr_budgeting_location_information_page.ifSkipped: Roll-ups are incorrect and fund reports misstate totals.

scr_budgeting_changing_the_parent_of_a_l.purpose: Moves a location under a different parent in the hierarchy — for example when a property moves to a different region or fund.
scr_budgeting_changing_the_parent_of_a_l.outcome: The property rolls into its new region or fund in reports going forward.
scr_budgeting_changing_the_parent_of_a_l.rootCause: Properties move between regions and funds after reorganizations or recapitalizations; the hierarchy must follow or reports show them in the old group.
scr_budgeting_changing_the_parent_of_a_l.ifSkipped: Regional and fund reports include properties that no longer belong to them.
redFlags: Parent changes mid-year affecting year-to-date comparisons

scr_budgeting_inactivating_a_location.purpose: Inactivates a location after a property is sold or management ends, preserving its history but preventing new budgets or postings.
scr_budgeting_inactivating_a_location.outcome: Sold properties stop appearing in active budgets while history is kept.
scr_budgeting_inactivating_a_location.rootCause: After disposition, the property must not receive new budgets or transactions, but its history is needed for final reporting and audits.
scr_budgeting_inactivating_a_location.ifSkipped: Sold properties appear in next year's budgets or receive stray postings.
redFlags: Inactivating before final closing entries are posted

scr_budgeting_setting_up_segments_for_fo.purpose: Sets up segments — additional user-defined classifications (e.g., renovation program, unit type, fund) — so budgets and actuals can be analyzed along them.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_segments_for_fo.outcome: Budgets can be sliced by owner-specific classifications without changing the chart of accounts.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_segments_for_fo.rootCause: Owners often want analysis by attributes like renovated vs classic units or capital program; segments provide that dimension without multiplying GL accounts.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_segments_for_fo.ifSkipped: Owner-requested analyses require manual tagging in spreadsheets.
redFlags: Segments enabled but not used consistently

scr_budgeting_segments.purpose: Describes segments as user-defined dimensions that tag transactions and budgets for analysis.
scr_budgeting_segments.outcome: Users understand when to use segments instead of new accounts.
scr_budgeting_segments.rootCause: Creating new GL accounts for every analysis need bloats the chart; segments are the intended tool for analytical tagging.
scr_budgeting_segments.ifSkipped: The chart of accounts is bloated with analysis-specific accounts.
redFlags: GL accounts created for purposes segments should serve

scr_budgeting_segments_overview.purpose: Overview of how segments work — segment types, values, and how they appear on transactions, budgets and reports.
scr_budgeting_segments_overview.outcome: A shared understanding of segments before enabling them.
scr_budgeting_segments_overview.rootCause: Segments affect data entry for every transaction once enabled; understanding them first prevents inconsistent tagging.
scr_budgeting_segments_overview.ifSkipped: Segments are enabled and tagged inconsistently, producing unreliable analysis.

scr_budgeting_enabling_segments.purpose: Enables segments in General Ledger configuration so they can be used on transactions and budgets.
scr_budgeting_enabling_segments.rootCause: Segments must be enabled centrally; partial enabling leads to some transactions tagged and others not.
scr_budgeting_enabling_segments.ifSkipped: Segment analysis is impossible or incomplete.
redFlags: Segments enabled mid-year without backfilling tags

scr_budgeting_reports_that_use_segments.purpose: Lists which financial and budget reports can filter or group by segments, so accountants know where segment tagging (e.g., renovated vs classic units) can actually be analyzed.
scr_budgeting_reports_that_use_segments.outcome: Users know where segment analysis is available.
scr_budgeting_reports_that_use_segments.rootCause: Tagging only has value if reports use it; knowing which reports support segments helps plan analysis.
scr_budgeting_reports_that_use_segments.ifSkipped: Segments are tagged diligently but never used in any report, wasting data-entry effort.
redFlags: Segment tagging with no reporting use

scr_budgeting_segments_list.purpose: Lists segment types (e.g., Renovation Status, Fund, Unit Type) and their values under Company > Segments, where segments are added and maintained for tagging budgets and transactions.
scr_budgeting_segments_list.outcome: A maintained catalog of segment values.
scr_budgeting_segments_list.rootCause: Uncontrolled segment values multiply and fragment analysis; a maintained list keeps tagging consistent.
scr_budgeting_segments_list.ifSkipped: Segment values proliferate and analysis becomes unreliable.

scr_budgeting_adding_segments.purpose: Adds segment types and their values — for example a 'Renovation Status' segment with values Classic, Renovated, In Progress.
scr_budgeting_adding_segments.outcome: New analysis dimensions available for tagging.
scr_budgeting_adding_segments.rootCause: New owner analyses (e.g., premium on renovated units) need new segments before tagging can begin.
scr_budgeting_adding_segments.ifSkipped: Requested analyses cannot be produced from system data.

scr_budgeting_importing_segments.purpose: Imports segment types and their values from a template through Company > Import Data, used when a new owner requires a segment with many values.
scr_budgeting_importing_segments.outcome: Large segment catalogs loaded in one step.
scr_budgeting_importing_segments.rootCause: Segments with many values (e.g., one per building) are impractical to key manually.
scr_budgeting_importing_segments.ifSkipped: Segment catalogs are incomplete or keyed with errors.
redFlags: Import not reconciled to the source list

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_segmen.purpose: Views or edits a segment type and its list of values — for example adding a new renovation phase value as a value-add program progresses.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_segmen.outcome: The segment catalog stays current with the programs it tracks.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_segmen.rootCause: As programs evolve (renovation phases), segment values must be updated for tagging to stay meaningful.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_segmen.ifSkipped: Segment values become outdated and misleading.
redFlags: Renaming values that change historical meaning

scr_budgeting_segment_information_page.purpose: The segment record page for adding, viewing or editing a segment type and its values.
scr_budgeting_segment_information_page.outcome: Each segment has a clear definition and complete list of values for consistent tagging.
scr_budgeting_segment_information_page.rootCause: Clear definitions and value lists are needed for consistent tagging by many users.
scr_budgeting_segment_information_page.ifSkipped: Users tag inconsistently and segment reports are unreliable.

scr_budgeting_importing_segment_values.purpose: Imports additional values into an existing segment type from a file — for example one value per building on a large garden-style campus.
scr_budgeting_importing_segment_values.rootCause: Adding many values (e.g., every building on a campus) by hand is slow and error-prone.
scr_budgeting_importing_segment_values.ifSkipped: Values are missing and transactions cannot be tagged.

scr_budgeting_searching_the_list_of_segm.purpose: Searches the value list of a segment type when adding or viewing values, so users can find the right value quickly in lists with hundreds of entries.
scr_budgeting_searching_the_list_of_segm.outcome: Faster tagging and maintenance for large segment lists.
scr_budgeting_searching_the_list_of_segm.rootCause: Segments with hundreds of values are unusable without search; wrong values get picked when users scroll.
scr_budgeting_searching_the_list_of_segm.ifSkipped: Users pick wrong values from long lists.
redFlags: Frequent retagging due to wrong value selection

scr_budgeting_appendices.purpose: Appendices to the Forecasting & Planning guide containing reference material, especially the import instructions used during budget season.
scr_budgeting_appendices.outcome: Reference instructions available for less frequent tasks like bulk imports.
scr_budgeting_appendices.rootCause: Budget imports happen once or twice a year, so staff rarely remember the steps; reference material prevents repeated errors.
scr_budgeting_appendices.ifSkipped: Import errors repeat each budget season.

scr_budgeting_importing.purpose: Appendix on importing data into RealPage for budgeting — templates, CSV preparation, the import process and error resolution.
scr_budgeting_importing.outcome: A reliable procedure for bulk-loading budgets and master data.
scr_budgeting_importing.rootCause: Most budgets are loaded by import; failed or partial imports are the main source of budget-in-system errors.
scr_budgeting_importing.ifSkipped: Budgets are loaded partially or incorrectly.
redFlags: Imports not reconciled to source totals

scr_budgeting_the_import_process.purpose: Describes the import process end to end: download template, fill data, save as CSV, upload, review results and fix errors.
scr_budgeting_the_import_process.outcome: Imports follow a consistent, checkable process.
scr_budgeting_the_import_process.rootCause: Skipping the review-results step is how partial loads slip through; a defined process makes it mandatory.
scr_budgeting_the_import_process.ifSkipped: Partial imports go unnoticed and budgets are missing lines that nobody knows failed to load.

scr_budgeting_downloading_a_template_fro.purpose: Downloads the import template for the record type (budgets, accounts, locations) from Company > Import Data.
scr_budgeting_downloading_a_template_fro.outcome: A correctly structured starting file for imports.
scr_budgeting_downloading_a_template_fro.rootCause: Templates carry required columns and formats; using old or custom files is the leading cause of import errors.
scr_budgeting_downloading_a_template_fro.ifSkipped: Imports fail or map columns incorrectly.
redFlags: Templates reused from previous years without refresh

scr_budgeting_filling_in_an_import_templ.purpose: Fills the import template with budget or master data following column rules (required fields, codes, date formats).
scr_budgeting_filling_in_an_import_templ.rootCause: Codes must match system values exactly (account numbers, location IDs); typos cause row rejections that are easy to miss.
scr_budgeting_filling_in_an_import_templ.ifSkipped: Rows are rejected and budgets are incomplete.
redFlags: Account numbers typed with extra spaces or formatting

scr_budgeting_preparing_your_csv_file_fo.purpose: Explains saving the template as CSV correctly — no formulas, correct encoding, no extra rows — before upload.
scr_budgeting_preparing_your_csv_file_fo.outcome: Files the importer can read reliably.
scr_budgeting_preparing_your_csv_file_fo.rootCause: Excel artifacts (formulas, hidden rows, formatted numbers) break CSV imports or silently change values such as leading zeros in account numbers.
scr_budgeting_preparing_your_csv_file_fo.ifSkipped: Imports fail or silently load altered values such as account codes with leading zeros removed.

scr_budgeting_importing_a_budget.purpose: Imports a complete budget from a CSV template — often the easiest way to load an owner-approved budget built in Excel.
scr_budgeting_importing_a_budget.outcome: The approved budget loaded into the system for BVA reporting.
scr_budgeting_importing_a_budget.rootCause: Owners approve budgets in Excel; importing that exact file ensures the system budget matches the approved one.
scr_budgeting_importing_a_budget.ifSkipped: The approved budget is re-keyed with errors or not loaded before January reporting.
redFlags: Imported totals not tied to the approved file

scr_budgeting_resolving_errors.purpose: Resolves import errors — reviewing rejected records, correcting them in the file and re-importing only the failed rows.
scr_budgeting_resolving_errors.outcome: All rows loaded without duplicating those that already succeeded.
scr_budgeting_resolving_errors.rootCause: Re-importing the whole file after a partial failure duplicates successful rows; correcting only failures prevents doubled budgets.
scr_budgeting_resolving_errors.ifSkipped: Budgets are either incomplete or duplicated.
redFlags: Full file re-imported after partial success

scr_budgeting_common_errors.purpose: Lists common import errors (invalid account or location codes, wrong date formats, missing required fields) and how to avoid them.
scr_budgeting_common_errors.outcome: Fewer import failures during budget season.
scr_budgeting_common_errors.rootCause: The same errors recur every season; a checklist of known pitfalls prevents them.
scr_budgeting_common_errors.ifSkipped: Budget loads fail repeatedly under deadline.

scr_budgeting_about_the_forecasting_and_.purpose: Quick Steps overview of Forecasting & Planning — building working budgets, calculating payroll and management fees, comparing versions and publishing the approved budget.
scr_budgeting_about_the_forecasting_and_.outcome: New staff understand the budget cycle in the system quickly.
scr_budgeting_about_the_forecasting_and_.rootCause: Budget season is short and new offshore staff often join mid-year; a condensed overview gets them productive before the deadline.
scr_budgeting_about_the_forecasting_and_.ifSkipped: New staff make structural mistakes during budget season.
redFlags: First-time preparers publishing budgets without review

scr_budgeting_setting_up_dimensions.purpose: Quick Steps for setting up dimensions (locations, departments, employees, vendors, customers) when the company uses them for budgeting.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_dimensions.outcome: Dimensions ready before budgets are built.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_dimensions.rootCause: Budgets by department or location need those dimensions in place first; a short checklist prevents starting budgets without them.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_dimensions.ifSkipped: Budgets must be rebuilt after dimensions are added.
redFlags: Dimensions added after budgets were built

scr_budgeting_setting_up_segments.purpose: Quick Steps for setting up segment types and values when segments are enabled, so budgets and transactions can be tagged for owner-specific analysis such as renovation premiums.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_segments.rootCause: Segments must exist before budgets and transactions can be tagged for owner-requested analysis.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_segments.ifSkipped: Segment analysis requested by owners cannot be produced.

scr_budgeting_adding_a_working_budget_2.purpose: Quick Steps for creating a working budget for properties and a fiscal year, choosing the seed (actuals, prior budget or blank).
scr_budgeting_adding_a_working_budget_2.outcome: A new draft budget ready for assumptions.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_working_budget_2.rootCause: Choosing the right seed is the first key decision of the budget; the quick path highlights it so drafts start from a sound base.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_working_budget_2.ifSkipped: Drafts start from the wrong seed and need rework.
redFlags: Seeded from partial-year actuals without annualizing

scr_budgeting_viewing_the_working_budget.purpose: Quick Steps for opening the working budget summary to review totals by account and period.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_working_budget.outcome: Fast top-level review of a draft.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_working_budget.rootCause: Reviewers need a fast way to check the headline totals — revenue growth, controllable expenses, NOI — before spending time on individual lines, because an unrealistic NOI invalidates line-level work.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_working_budget.ifSkipped: Unrealistic totals are missed while reviewing lines.

scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_to_a_wor.purpose: Quick Steps for adding an account that the seed did not include to a working budget.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_to_a_wor.outcome: New revenue or cost activities are included in the draft budget.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_to_a_wor.rootCause: Seeds miss accounts without history; new revenue or cost lines must be added explicitly.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_to_a_wor.ifSkipped: New activities are unbudgeted and create variances all year.

scr_budgeting_publishing_a_working_budge.purpose: Quick Steps for publishing the approved working budget to the GL budget used in BVA reports and budget checks.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_working_budge.outcome: The owner-approved budget is live in the GL.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_working_budge.rootCause: Publishing is the control point between drafts and official reporting; a clear procedure prevents publishing the wrong draft or target.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_working_budge.ifSkipped: BVA runs against the wrong budget or no budget at all.

scr_budgeting_calculating_the_budget_inc.purpose: Quick Steps for applying a percentage or amount increase to an account's budget base.
scr_budgeting_calculating_the_budget_inc.rootCause: Escalators are the most common budget adjustment; a quick procedure ensures they are applied to the right base.
scr_budgeting_calculating_the_budget_inc.ifSkipped: Escalators are applied to the wrong base and the budget line is over- or understated.

scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.purpose: Quick Steps for adjusting one account's working budget by an amount or percentage after review feedback, with a comment recording why.
scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.rootCause: Review feedback usually targets specific lines; a quick adjustment path keeps review rounds moving.
scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.ifSkipped: Review feedback is applied late or not at all, and the published budget differs from what was agreed.

scr_budgeting_advancing_year_to_date_act.purpose: Quick Steps for bringing year-to-date actuals into a reforecast so completed months show actual results.
scr_budgeting_advancing_year_to_date_act.outcome: A reforecast anchored on reported actuals.
scr_budgeting_advancing_year_to_date_act.rootCause: Reforecasts shared with investors must reconcile to reported results; advancing actuals from the GL ensures it.
scr_budgeting_advancing_year_to_date_act.ifSkipped: Reforecast actuals differ from reported financials.

scr_budgeting_comparing_budgets_in_the_w.purpose: Quick Steps for comparing two budget versions, or a budget with actuals, in the workbench.
scr_budgeting_comparing_budgets_in_the_w.rootCause: Asset managers want to see what changed between drafts; a quick comparison procedure makes that easy.
scr_budgeting_comparing_budgets_in_the_w.ifSkipped: Changes between drafts go unexplained and the asset manager loses confidence in the budget.

scr_budgeting_adding_and_calculating_a_p.purpose: Quick Steps for creating a property's payroll budget and calculating wages, taxes, benefits and workers' comp.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_calculating_a_p.outcome: A calculated payroll budget ready to publish.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_calculating_a_p.rootCause: Payroll is the largest controllable expense; a short procedure keeps calculation consistent across properties.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_calculating_a_p.ifSkipped: Payroll is estimated inconsistently across properties and cannot be explained line by line.

scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_to_a_pa.purpose: Quick Steps for adding an employee or a planned open position to a property's payroll budget, such as a seasonal pool attendant or an additional maintenance technician.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_to_a_pa.rootCause: Staffing plans change during budget season; the quick path keeps the payroll budget aligned.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_to_a_pa.ifSkipped: Planned hires are missing from payroll and the property's payroll is under-budgeted.
redFlags: Additions not approved by the regional manager

scr_budgeting_publishing_a_payroll_to_a_.purpose: Quick Steps for publishing a calculated payroll into the working budget's payroll accounts.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_payroll_to_a_.outcome: Operating budget payroll matches the payroll model.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_payroll_to_a_.rootCause: Publishing links payroll detail to the operating budget; forgetting it leaves stale payroll lines.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_payroll_to_a_.ifSkipped: Operating budget payroll differs from the model.

scr_budgeting_calculating_management_fee.purpose: Quick Steps for calculating budgeted management fees from budgeted revenue and the contract percentage.
scr_budgeting_calculating_management_fee.outcome: Fee budgets consistent with revenue and the management agreement.
scr_budgeting_calculating_management_fee.rootCause: Fees must move with revenue; recalculating after revenue changes keeps the budget consistent.
scr_budgeting_calculating_management_fee.ifSkipped: Fee budgets do not match final revenue and the budget is internally inconsistent.
redFlags: Fee base inconsistent with the agreement

scr_budgeting_publishing_management_fees.purpose: Quick Steps for publishing the calculated management fee into the management fee account of the working budget after revenue assumptions are final.
scr_budgeting_publishing_management_fees.outcome: Fee lines in the budget match the calculation.
scr_budgeting_publishing_management_fees.rootCause: Publishing links fee calculations to the budget; skipping it leaves stale fee lines after revenue changes.
scr_budgeting_publishing_management_fees.ifSkipped: Budget fee lines are inconsistent with revenue.
redFlags: Fees not republished after revenue revisions
